headline: Current account surplus plunges almost 55%, driven by rising energy prices
summary: Spain's net lending capacity fell to 3.3% of GDP as rising energy prices weighed on the current account surplus. Record household and business savings partly offset the decline.
why: The current account balance measures a country's net trade and income flows with the rest of the world, which matters for its external financing needs and currency. Spain is a large eurozone economy.
